summary: Binary approval policy over typed JEV judgments: confirmed hazards deny, a hazard signal below the action threshold does not by itself deny, and a bounded low-or-medium-risk action with adequate authorization allows. An incomplete or invalid verdict allows: deny requires positive evidence.

deny_rules.when: risk_level == critical, even inside an otherwise invalid or partial verdict
violates_explicit_constraint is present, valid, and >= action_probability
malicious_instruction is present, valid, and >= action_probability
persistent_security_weakening is present, valid, and >= action_probability
sensitive_egress is present, valid, and >= action_probability AND egress_authorized is absent, invalid, or < action_probability
a composed allow was computed against an authorization version that provably changed while the review was in flight
effective risk is high (risk_level == high OR credential_probing >= action_probability OR destructive_effect >= action_probability) AND user_authorization is neither medium nor high
effective risk is high AND narrowly_scoped < action_probability

degradation: an unavailable assessor, an API failure, an invalid or incomplete verdict, unverifiable authorization freshness, or an unavailable audit store all resolve to allow — this gate is the harness's auto mode, so a reviewer that cannot produce a verdict must not stall the user's work; degraded allows are recorded with incomplete: true
evaluation_order: positive-evidence deny rules evaluate on whatever fields are present and valid, before completeness checks; if no rule matches — including when the verdict is missing or invalid — the outcome is allow
notes: thresholds uncalibrated — no validated dataset yet
